about: The CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model v2.0 (five pillars — Identity, Devices, Networks, Applications & Workloads, Data — and the three cross-cutting capabilities) assessed against what the SecuRAX estate demonstrably does. SecuRAX RUNS and GOVERNS an AI estate, a cyber range and a personal Life OS on one box; it is not an endpoint-management (MDM/EDR) product, so several device-pillar functions belong to the organisation that owns the laptops and phones, not to this software. Each title is CISA's function name; the notes are our own assessment and can be wrong: challenge them.

source.title: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model v2.0
source.issued: US Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), April 2023
source.caveat: Pillar and function names are from CISA's published model; the four maturity stages (Traditional/Initial/Advanced/Optimal) are not scored per-stage here. Status is our own judgement of a single-box lab estate, not a CISA assessment.

items.title: Identity · Authentication
items.note: The gateway authenticates every caller when auth is on: per-caller service keys, anonymous and wrong keys refused, repeated failures lock the source out, and the open-laptop default is explicit.

items.title: Identity · Identity Stores
items.note: Service identities and roles live with the gateway, and Open WebUI can trust a verified sign-in header on loopback; there is no central IdP wired by default.
items.next: Offer optional OIDC sign-in through the gateway's identity so one IdP backs every surface (tracked as studio-harden / gateway identity).

items.title: Identity · Risk Assessments
items.note: Behavioural signals (request bursts, odd-hour activity) raise an alarm; a new model alone no longer does. There is no continuous, real-time identity-risk score.
items.next: Add a continuous identity-risk score that adjusts access as signals change.

items.title: Identity · Access Management
items.note: Roles limit what a key can reach and lockout bounds abuse, so access is scoped at provisioning; it is not yet just-in-time / just-enough.
items.next: Add just-in-time, just-enough access that expires, instead of standing role grants.

items.title: Devices · Policy Enforcement & Compliance Monitoring
items.note: SecuRAX hardens and monitors its OWN containers (non-root, no-new-privileges, digest pins), but endpoint posture on the laptops and phones is the organisation's MDM to enforce, not this software's.

items.title: Devices · Asset & Supply Chain Risk Management
items.note: Strong for the estate's SOFTWARE supply chain — third-party code is vetted and pinned, and anything new is inspected in a sandbox before trust — but device/hardware inventory is the organisation's.
items.next: Device and hardware asset inventory remains an organisation/MDM responsibility, outside this box.

items.title: Devices · Resource Access (device-based)
items.note: Access decisions do not yet consider the requesting device's posture.
items.next: Let the edge consider a device-posture signal before granting access to estate surfaces.

items.title: Devices · Device Threat Protection
items.note: Endpoint threat protection (EDR/anti-malware on the user's devices) belongs to the organisation; SecuRAX protects the estate it runs, not the endpoints that reach it.

items.title: Networks · Network Segmentation
items.note: Services bind to loopback and talk over named, internal-only Docker networks (edge / modelplane / internal); the cyber range runs on fully isolated zones with no way out to the internet or LAN.

items.title: Networks · Network Traffic Management
items.note: One HTTPS edge routes by name (hub./chat./api. …) on port 443; residency routing steers a request to the right model by its data.

items.title: Networks · Traffic Encryption
items.note: TLS on every web connection at the edge, and, with internal TLS on, every service-to-service hop goes through a per-service sidecar so plain HTTP between containers is refused.

items.title: Networks · Network Resilience
items.note: A resilient model ladder fails over rung to rung, components self-heal after a kill, and the estate still comes up and answers with a machine, a peer and the network removed.

items.title: Applications & Workloads · Application Access
items.note: Access to the AI gateway is authenticated and role-limited, and a write from a foreign origin is refused (CORS hides the answer but the request is still blocked).

items.title: Applications & Workloads · Application Threat Protections
items.note: Input and output rails block prompt injection, jailbreaks, hidden-character smuggling, secret and PII leakage; an optional detector adds model-based safety; the red team scores it on every change.

items.title: Applications & Workloads · Accessible Applications (safely exposed, not public)
items.note: Everything binds to loopback by default and is reached by name through the one HTTPS edge; code-running add-ons (Studio) are password-gated and never part of the core start.

items.title: Applications & Workloads · Secure Application Development & Deployment Workflow
items.note: Every change passes a gate that cannot be faked green — a diff-honesty check rejects an agent that 'passes' by skipping a test, and the forge gate classifies real failures — before it can merge.

items.title: Applications & Workloads · Application Security Testing
items.note: CI runs SAST and secret scanning, container and IaC scanning, and third-party vetting on every PR; a test proves those security jobs are actually wired (an unparsable workflow can't silently skip them).

items.title: Data · Data Inventory Management
items.note: The estate knows its sensitive data where it matters — India identity numbers (Aadhaar/PAN) are detected, secret columns are dropped on import, and storage is bounded by tier — but there is no full data catalogue.
items.next: Add a lightweight data catalogue that lists where each class of data lives and its retention tier.

items.title: Data · Data Categorization
items.note: Data is classified where it drives a decision — PII and secrets are recognised by the rails, and residency marks India-local data — but there is no general labelling scheme.
items.next: Add explicit sensitivity labels that follow data through the estate.

items.title: Data · Data Availability
items.note: Backups are checked before they are taken (ransomguard), kept as weeks and months not just a count, copied off-site, and a destroy-and-restore drill proves the data really comes back.

items.title: Data · Data Access
items.note: Residency routing keeps India-local data off cloud models and says why in the audit; roles bound what a caller can reach; an out-of-policy region or an unattested cloud is refused.

items.title: Data · Data Encryption
items.note: Backups are AES-256 encrypted with a key kept off the box (quantum-safe, no public-key step), a wrong key or tampered file is refused before anything is touched, and data in transit is TLS.

items.title: Cross-cutting · Visibility & Analytics
items.note: Every AI call is written to a tamper-evident audit chain; one cockpit page shows live risks and health; a watchdog proves readiness and alerts; offline threat intel (KEV/ATT&CK/EPSS) answers with no network.

items.title: Cross-cutting · Automation & Orchestration
items.note: Scheduled routines, self-healing on failure, and a single incident detection that starts the regulator reporting clock for RBI, SEBI and CERT-In together — security response runs without a person watching.

items.title: Cross-cutting · Governance
items.note: One source of principles propagates to every app; every feature declares its edition and platform services; a requirement-by-requirement compliance view and a checksummed evidence pack make policy enforceable and auditable; one switch turns on sign-in, residency and a strict cockpit.
